source.title: Geometric Bogomolov conjecture in arbitrary characteristics
source.version: arXiv v1 (22 August 2021, 29 pages), the only arXiv version, read completely; the Inventiones article (received 31 August 2021) is subscription-only and was not collated.
readSections: 2026-09-29: arXiv:2108.09722v1, all 29 pages: §§1–5 and references; page images checked at every source issue.
2026-09-30, Codex codex-J6LwjP: focused fix reading of arXiv v1 pp.1–3, 7, 9–11, 13–27; page images checked at pp.13, 16, 17, 25. This is not a new full-paper reading.

summary: Xie and Yuan prove the geometric Bogomolov conjecture in full: over a finitely generated K/k (k algebraically closed, any characteristic), a subvariety of an abelian variety with a dense set of small points is special. §3 lowers the transcendence degree to 1 without changing K, by passing to generic hyperplane sections over subfields k′ ⊂ K and tracking where X becomes special through fields of definition. Yamaki's theorem then reduces to good reduction and trivial trace. There §4 shows a torsion multi-section is numerically a multiple of ℒ^{dim A}, and §2's inequality for non-proper intersections bounds the dominant part of f⁻¹(𝒯) for the summation map f : X_{r−1} × X → X_r. So fibres over torsion points have height 0, are torsion by induction, and Manin–Mumford finishes. The atlas has no function-field Bogomolov theorem: the core goes to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions, beside Gao–Habegger's characteristic-0 case. Heights, trace and Manin–Mumford inputs go to RP.0/RP.1/RP.5, the intersection theory to SchemeAndStackFoundations, and the line-bundle lemmas to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.

items.name: Abelian varieties, products and base change
items.statement: An abelian variety over a field K is a proper, geometrically integral group scheme over K; products A × A, B × C and base change A_{K̄} = A ⊗_K K̄ are taken in this category.
items.note: Tau Ceti's structure bundles a group object over Spec K with IsProper and GeometricallyIntegral, the paper's notion over a field. Abelian schemes over a curve (§4) are not in either library; they are AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1.

items.name: Multiplication by n on an abelian variety
items.statement: For n ∈ Z, [n] : A → A is multiplication by n; [n]X denotes the image of a subvariety X.
items.note: Over a field only. That [n] is an isogeny for n ≠ 0 is not yet in Tau Ceti (the audit of JacobianChallenge layer E records only [−1]); the relative [m] on an abelian scheme and A[m] are A3.

items.name: Isogenies and the relation A₁ ∼ A₂
items.statement: An isogeny is a finite surjective homomorphism of abelian varieties; A₁ ∼ A₂ if A₁ is isogenous to A₂.
items.note: Tau Ceti defines isogenies over a field as finite surjective homomorphisms, with composition and base change. Symmetry of ∼ needs a quasi-inverse isogeny, which is not there yet; for isogenies of abelian schemes the paper's relation over a base is AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3.

items.name: Transcendence degree
items.statement: trdeg(K/k) is the transcendence degree of the field extension K/k.

items.name: Projective models, polarizations and integral models
items.statement: For K/k finitely generated with k algebraically closed and trdeg(K/k) ≥ 1: a projective model of K/k is a normal projective variety S over k with function field K (so dim S = trdeg(K/k)); a polarization of K/k is a pair (S, M) with S a projective model and M an ample line bundle on S. For an abelian variety A over K with a symmetric ample line bundle L, an integral model of (A, L) over S is (𝒜, π, ℒ) with 𝒜 a projective variety over k, π : 𝒜 → S projective with generic fibre A, and ℒ a line bundle on 𝒜 extending L.
items.note: Geometric (function-field) height data over a finitely generated field. RP.0 plans number-field heights only; routed to RP.0 as a source, as PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 did for the curve case.

items.name: Naive height of a subvariety, (1.1)
items.statement: For a closed subvariety X of A, h^M_{(𝒜,ℒ)}(X) := ℒ^{dim X+1} · (π*M)^{dim S−1} · 𝒳 / ((1 + dim X) deg_L(X)), where 𝒳 is the Zariski closure of X in 𝒜, the numerator is an intersection number on 𝒜 and deg_L(X) = L^{dim X} · X on A.
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Canonical height of subvarieties, (1.2)–(1.3)
items.statement: ĥ^M_L(X) := lim_{n→∞} n^{−2} h_{(𝒜,ℒ)}([n]X) exists, depends on (S, M) and L but not on the integral model (Gubler 2007, Thm. 3.6; Gubler 2003, Thm. 11.18), and ĥ^M_L(X) ≥ 0 (take ℒ ample). For a closed subvariety X′ of A_{K̄}, set ĥ(X′) := ĥ(X) with X the image of X′ → A_{K̄} → A; for points this gives ĥ : A(K̄) → [0, ∞). When trdeg(K/k) = 1 the model S is unique and M plays no role.
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source; the existence and independence are cited inputs from Gubler, listed as prerequisites. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: Canonical height of a sum
items.statement: For x₁, …, x_m ∈ A(K̄), ĥ(x₁ + ⋯ + x_m) ≤ m(ĥ(x₁) + ⋯ + ĥ(x_m)), since ĥ is a positive semi-definite quadratic form on A(K̄).
items.note: The function-field Néron–Tate height as a quadratic form; routed to RP.0 with the other function-field heights. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: Canonical height under good reduction, §4.3
items.statement: Let S be a smooth projective curve over k, K = k(S), and A/K with everywhere good reduction, 𝒜 → S the abelian scheme extending it. A symmetric ample L on A extends to a symmetric rigidified ℒ on 𝒜 (extend any divisor, subtract π*e*ℒ′; symmetry then follows from the rigidification). For a closed subvariety X with closure 𝒳, h_ℒ(X) = ℒ^{dim X+1} · 𝒳 / ((dim X + 1) deg_L(X)) satisfies h_ℒ([n]X) = n² h_ℒ(X), hence equals ĥ(X).
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source (function-field heights), with Lemma 4.1(1) from A1 as its input. Use generic-trivial-line-bundle (SF.0, shared DGH21/29) to show ℒ−[−1]*ℒ is pulled back from S and then trivial by rigidification. Use abelian-scheme-projectivity (A2, shared DGH21/26) for a projective model and an ample symmetric rigidified extension when needed. The arbitrary generic bundle’s extension is obtained on the regular total space; the model/canonical comparison is model-mk-height.

items.name: Height zero means torsion when the trace is trivial
items.statement: If A over a finitely generated K/k has trivial K/k-trace, then x ∈ A(K̄) has ĥ(x) = 0 if and only if x is torsion (Northcott property; Conrad 2006, Thm. 9.15).
items.locator: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Lemma 5.3, p. 24; §5.3, p. 26
items.note: The kernel of the function-field Néron–Tate height, which combines Lang–Néron with Northcott; routed to RP.0 as a source as in PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: The K/k-trace
items.statement: The K/k-trace (A^{K̄/k}, tr) of A_{K̄} is the final object among pairs (C, f) with C an abelian variety over k and f : C ⊗_k K̄ → A_{K̄} (Lang; Conrad 2006, §6). If char k = 0, tr is a closed immersion; if char k > 0, tr is a purely inseparable isogeny onto its image.
items.note: Routed with Lang–Néron to RP.1 as a source, as in PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19. The paper also uses that sub- and quotient abelian varieties of a trivial-trace A have trivial trace (proof of Lemma 5.3).

items.name: Torsion subvarieties
items.statement: A torsion subvariety of A_{K̄} is a translate a + C of an abelian subvariety C ⊂ A_{K̄} by a torsion point a.
items.note: RP.5 constructs translates and treats torsion translates as the special components of Manin–Mumford. Use prime-to-p-torsion-density (A3). In §5.3 it supplies the dense set of admissible base points off A′_{e+1} and, after translation, dense all-torsion points in each torsion fibre component.

items.name: Stabilizer of a subvariety
items.statement: Stab(X) = {g ∈ A : g + X = X} is a closed subgroup scheme of A; Stab⁰(X) is its identity component.
items.note: RP.5: 'Construct translates, stabilizers and finitely generated subgroup intersections'.

items.name: Quotients by abelian subvarieties and the minimal torsion subvariety
items.statement: For an abelian subvariety B ⊂ A there is a quotient abelian variety A → A/B; X/Stab⁰(X) denotes the image of X. For a subvariety X, T_X is the minimal torsion subvariety of A containing X; for a torsion point a ∈ T_X, T_X − a is an abelian subvariety.
items.locator: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Proposition 3.6, p. 16; proof of Lemma 5.3, p. 24
items.note: A3 plans quotients by finite locally free subgroups only. Routed to RP.5 as a source beside its translates and stabilizers.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (Manin–Mumford conjecture, trivial trace)
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated over an algebraically closed field k, and A an abelian variety over K with trivial K/k-trace. If X ⊂ A_{K̄} is a closed subvariety with X(K̄) ∩ A(K̄)_tor Zariski dense in X, then X is a torsion subvariety (Raynaud over number fields; Hrushovski 2001 in general; Pink–Roessler 2002/2004).
items.note: RP.5 plans the Manin–Mumford theorem 'with precise characteristic and field hypotheses'; the positive-characteristic, trivial-trace case needs Hrushovski's or Pink–Roessler's proof, which no layer names. Routed to RP.5 as a source; PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 marked the characteristic-0 case planned there. Added by REV-PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22: in positive characteristic a version covering all torsion, including p-power torsion, is Pink–Roessler (J. Algebraic Geom. 13 (2004), the paper's [PR04]) and Scanlon, Positive characteristic Manin–Mumford theorem (arXiv:math/0303340, Theorem 2.2): the Zariski closure of X ∩ G_tor is a finite union of 'special' subvarieties a + h⁻¹(X₀) with h: G → G₀ and X₀ defined over F̄_p. With trivial K/k-trace there is no nonzero homomorphism to an abelian variety over F̄_p ⊆ k, so these are torsion translates and Theorem 5.1 follows; the blueprint should derive it that way. Use prime-to-p-torsion-density (A3). In §5.3 it supplies the dense set of admissible base points off A′_{e+1} and, after translation, dense all-torsion points in each torsion fibre component.

items.name: Chow groups with rational coefficients and effectivity
items.statement: For a smooth projective variety B of dimension d over algebraically closed k and an i-cycle Z with Q-coefficients, [Z] ∈ CH_i(B)_Q is its class; α ≥ 0 means α is represented by an effective i-cycle.
items.note: SF.5 plans Chow groups, flat pullback and intersection products. Mathlib has algebraic cycles (AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle) but no rational equivalence.

items.name: Numerical equivalence of 1-cycles
items.statement: Two 1-cycles on 𝒜 are numerically equivalent (≡) if they have the same intersection number with every line bundle.

items.name: Serre intersection multiplicities and proper intersections
items.statement: For proper intersections on a smooth variety B, Serre’s alternating Tor-length intersection multiplicity agrees with the intersection product multiplicity. Successive Cartier-divisor intersections satisfy associativity of multiplicities. When the higher Tor terms vanish (in particular the regular-sequence/complete-intersection application in Proposition 2.1), the multiplicity equals the length of the local ring of the scheme-theoretic intersection (Fulton Proposition 7.1(b)); proper intersection alone is not a general Tor-vanishing hypothesis.
items.locator: arXiv:2108.09722v1, §2.2, p. 9; proof of Proposition 2.1, p. 11
items.note: SF.5 plans intersection products; the length formula for proper intersections is part of that construction. SF.5 must supply the agreement of Serre’s Tor multiplicity and Fulton’s multiplicity for proper intersections on a smooth ambient variety (Fulton §20.4 and Proposition 7.1), and associativity for successive Cartier divisors, which is the step in Proposition 2.4. The length-only shortcut requires vanishing of the higher Tor terms, as in the complete-intersection application on p.11; it is not valid for every proper intersection. Keep this planned input together; no duplicate missing Tor/associativity items are introduced.

items.name: Nef line bundles and positivity of intersections
items.statement: A line bundle is nef if its degree on every curve is ≥ 0. Intersections of nef bundles with effective cycles are ≥ 0; a limit of ample Q-line bundles is nef; if ℒ − ℒ′ is nef and ℒ′, ℳ nef then the corresponding top intersections with an effective cycle are ordered.
items.locator: arXiv:2108.09722v1, Lemma 4.1(3)–(4), p. 20; proofs of Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 5.4, pp. 18, 26
items.note: No layer plans nefness on higher-dimensional varieties (StableReduction treats curves). Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (Bertini-type choice of hypersurfaces through V)
items.statement: Let Y be projective over algebraically closed k, V ⊂ Y a closed subvariety of codimension r ≥ 1 with Y smooth at η_V, and Z₁, …, Z_m irreducible subvarieties with (∪Z_i) ∩ V finite and contained in Y^sm ∩ V^sm. Let H be a Cartier divisor with O_Y(H) ⊗ I_V globally generated. For general (s₁, …, s_r) ∈ H⁰(O_Y(H) ⊗ I_V)^r: (i) H_{s₁} ∩ ⋯ ∩ H_{s_r} is a proper intersection; (ii) H_{s₁} ⋯ H_{s_r} = V + W with W an effective (dim Y − r)-cycle, V ⊄ Supp W, and W ∩ Z_i proper for every i.
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.3
items.statement: Let B be smooth projective of dimension d over algebraically closed k and H a Cartier divisor with O_B(H) globally generated. For α ∈ CH_i(B)_Q with α ≥ 0, α · [H] ≥ 0.
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proper part of an intersection
items.statement: For Cartier divisors H₁, …, H_m and a subvariety X of smooth projective B, a proper component of H₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ H_m ∩ X is an irreducible component of dimension dim X − m, and (H₁ ⋯ H_m · X)^prop := Σ m(Z, H₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ H_m ∩ X)[Z] over the proper components Z.
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.4 (proper part is bounded by the intersection)
items.statement: If H₁, …, H_r are effective Cartier divisors on B with O_B(H_i) globally generated and X is a subvariety of B, then (H₁ ⋯ H_r · X)^prop ≤ H₁ ⋯ H_r · X.
items.note: Generalizes Jia–Shibata–Xie–Zhang, Lemma 3.3; a special case of Fulton's positivity for globally generated bundles (Intersection Theory, Thm. 12.2). The last display of the proof has V for X (sourceIssues E6). Routed to SF.5 as a source. The induction on Cartier divisors uses the associativity and Tor/product comparison explicitly named in intersection-multiplicity (SF.5).

items.name: Loci of large fibre dimension
items.statement: For f : X → Y surjective between projective varieties and e = dim X − dim Y, the sets Y_l = {y : dim f⁻¹(y) ≥ l} (l ≥ e) are closed, Y_{l+1} ⊆ Y_l, Y_e = Y, dim Y_l + l ≤ dim X − 1 for l ≥ e + 1, and Y_l = ∅ for l ≥ dim X.
items.note: Upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension (Chevalley); routed to SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.5
items.statement: Let W be a subvariety of Y with W ∩ Y_l proper for every l ≥ e + 1. Then dim f⁻¹(W) = dim W + e, and every irreducible component Z of f⁻¹(W) with dim Z = dim f⁻¹(W) satisfies f(Z) = W.
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.1, first part (dimension of the dominant components)
items.statement: Let g : B → Y be a flat morphism of smooth projective varieties over algebraically closed k, X ⊂ B a closed subvariety with f = g|_X surjective, e = dim X − dim Y, and V ⊂ Y a closed subvariety not contained in Y_{e+1}. If Z₁, …, Z_n are the irreducible components of f⁻¹(V) with f(Z_i) = V, then dim Z_i = dim V + e.
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.1, second part (non-proper intersection inequality)
items.statement: If moreover V ∩ Y_{e+1} is finite and contained in V^sm, then Σ m_i [Z_i] ≤ g*[V] · [X] in CH_{dim V+e}(B)_Q, with m_i the multiplicity of Z_i in f⁻¹(V). If X is smooth this reads Σ m_i Z_i ≤ f*[V] in CH_{dim V+e}(X)_Q.
items.note: Proof: Proposition 2.2 gives very ample H₁, …, H_r with H₁ ⋯ H_r = V + W, W meeting each Y_l properly; then [f⁻¹W] = g*[W] · [X] away from g⁻¹(V), and Proposition 2.4 bounds the proper part. Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Bertini: a general hyperplane section is geometrically integral
items.statement: For a very ample M on a projective variety S of dimension ≥ 2 over algebraically closed k, div(s₀) is geometrically integral for general s₀ ∈ Γ(S, M) (Jouanolou 1983, Thm. 6.10).
items.note: No layer plans Bertini irreducibility (LPV.3 treats Lefschetz pencils); routed to SF.5 as a source, as PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 did with its Bertini theorems.

items.name: Resolving a pencil by blowing up its base locus
items.statement: For s₀, s₁ ∈ Γ(S, M) spanning a pencil with base locus H₀ ∩ H₁, the blow-up π : S̃ → S along H₀ ∩ H₁ turns x ↦ (s₀(x) : s₁(x)) into a flat morphism ψ : S̃ → P¹_k (Hartshorne II, Ex. 7.17.3). For every field F/k and t ∈ P¹(F), the fibre ψ⁻¹(t) ⊂ S̃_F is isomorphic to the corresponding member div(a₀s₁ − a₁s₀) of the pencil, since H₀ ∩ H₁ is Cartier in each member.
items.note: SF.4 must supply the Rees-algebra blow-up of a closed subscheme over any field, with projective universal property and the pencil/graph comparison used here. R09.7a sits inside the characteristic-zero resolution scope R09.7 and cannot be assumed to discharge this all-characteristic input. Coalesce the underlying Rees-algebra construction with it only after an explicit scope extension/characteristic-independent supplier is approved. LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.3 is the smooth-axis special case; prove agreement there, without requiring smoothness of this paper’s base locus.

items.name: Geometric integrality spreads to the generic fibre
items.statement: For a flat proper morphism to P¹_k with a geometrically integral closed fibre, the generic fibre is geometrically integral; its base field is then algebraically closed in the function field.
items.note: Openness of the geometrically integral locus for proper flat morphisms (EGA IV₃ 12.2.4). Routed to SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Symmetric, anti-symmetric and rigidified line bundles
items.statement: For an abelian scheme π : 𝒜 → S with identity e, a line bundle ℒ is symmetric if [−1]*ℒ ≃ ℒ, anti-symmetric if [−1]*ℒ ≃ ℒ^∨, and rigidified if it carries an isomorphism e*ℒ ≃ O_S. ℳ − π*e*ℳ is canonically rigidified.
items.locator: arXiv:2108.09722v1, §4.1, p. 19; proof of Proposition 4.2, p. 21
items.note: A2 plans the rigidified Poincaré bundle but not this vocabulary for line bundles on an abelian scheme. Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1/A2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.1(1)
items.statement: Let ℒ be a rigidified line bundle on an abelian scheme 𝒜 over a smooth projective curve S. If ℒ is symmetric, [m]*ℒ ≃ m²ℒ for all m ∈ Z; if anti-symmetric, [m]*ℒ ≃ mℒ.
items.note: From the theorem of the cube fibrewise plus the rigidification. Routed to A1 (theorem of the cube) as a source. Use seesaw (A1) with the reduced curve base to turn fibrewise triviality into pullback from S; rigidification kills that pullback. A1’s full relative cube theorem is an alternative supplier.

items.name: Lemma 4.1(2)
items.statement: For a rigidified ℒ and any torsion multi-section 𝒯 ⊂ 𝒜, ℒ|_𝒯 is torsion in Pic(𝒯).
items.note: Proof: split 2ℒ into symmetric and anti-symmetric parts; ([m]*ℒ)|_{𝒜[m]} is trivial by the rigidification. Routed to A1 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.1(3)
items.statement: If ℒ is symmetric, rigidified and π-ample, then ℒ is nef on 𝒜.
items.note: Proof: ℒ + m⁻²π*L′ is ample for all m, so its limit ℒ is nef. Routed to A2 as a source. Use relative-to-absolute-ample (R09.1), multiplication-degree (A3) and finite-pullback-ample (SF.0). For nonzero m with |m|→∞, m²ℒ+π*N is ample; dividing by m² and taking the limit gives nefness. No assertion about [0] being finite is used.

items.name: Lemma 4.1(4)
items.statement: If ℒ is symmetric, rigidified and π-ample and ℒ′ is another symmetric rigidified line bundle, then aℒ − ℒ′ is nef for some positive integer a.
items.note: Routed to A2 as a source.

items.name: Torsion of order prime to the characteristic is finite étale
items.statement: If m is not divisible by char k, 𝒜[m] is finite étale over S; hence a torsion multi-section of order m is finite étale over S and smooth over k.
items.note: A3: '[n] is finite locally free of rank n^(2g) … and is étale precisely under the appropriate invertibility condition'.

items.name: Poincaré complete reducibility
items.statement: For an abelian subvariety B ⊂ A there is a surjective homomorphism A → B whose composite with B → A is an isogeny; hence A is isogenous to B × A/B.

items.name: Good reduction gives an abelian scheme
items.statement: Let S be a smooth projective integral curve over an algebraically closed field k of any characteristic, K=k(S), and A/K have everywhere good reduction. Its Néron model 𝒜→S is an abelian scheme, unique with the specified generic-fibre identification. A homomorphism between generic fibres of such models extends uniquely to a homomorphism over S. No closed-immersion assertion for extensions of inclusions is part of this statement.
items.locator: arXiv:2108.09722v1, §4.3, p. 21; proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 25
items.note: R11.1 supplies existence, uniqueness, good-reduction/model comparison and the mapping property. The removed closure clause is false in characteristic p (E16). The additional preservation of good reduction for a subvariety A′ and quotient is the separate item good-reduction-subquotients, shared with PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/80 at derived R11.5, whose planned isogeny-invariance theorem is used there. R11.1 must not depend on its downstream R11.5. Over a curve in characteristic zero the extended inclusion is closed; the stronger exactness statement is PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/81 and is not imported into the arbitrary-characteristic argument.

items.name: Semistable reduction theorem
items.statement: After a finite extension of K, A has semistable reduction over S.

items.name: Small points and dense sets of small points, (1.4)
items.statement: For a subvariety X of A_{K̄} and ε > 0, X(ε) := {x ∈ X(K̄) : ĥ(x) < ε}. X contains a dense set of small points of A/K/k if X(ε) is Zariski dense in X for all ε > 0; this is independent of L and (S, M), since any two such heights bound each other up to positive multiples.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: Special subvarieties, (1.5) and (3.3)
items.statement: A subvariety X of A_{K̄} is special (in A/K/k) if X = tr(Y ⊗_k K̄) + T for a torsion subvariety T of A_{K̄} and a subvariety Y of A^{K̄/k}. For K/k with k algebraically closed in K (not necessarily algebraically closed), (3.3) uses the same formula with k̄ and K̄.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Special subvarieties have dense small points
items.statement: If X is special then X(ε) is Zariski dense in X for every ε > 0 (Lang, Fundamentals of Diophantine Geometry, Ch. 6, Thm. 5.4).
items.note: The easy converse of Theorem 1.1; routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72. Use prime-to-p-torsion-density (A3). In §5.3 it supplies the dense set of admissible base points off A′_{e+1} and, after translation, dense all-torsion points in each torsion fibre component.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (geometric Bogomolov conjecture)
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated of transcendence degree ≥ 1, A an abelian variety over K and X a closed subvariety of A_{K̄}. If X contains a dense set of small points of A/K/k, then X is special.
items.note: Proved in all characteristics: Proposition 3.1 reduces to trdeg 1, Yamaki's theorem to good reduction and trivial trace, and §5 concludes by Manin–Mumford. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II, which already holds the characteristic-0 case over curves (PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19).

items.name: Abelian varieties defined over a subfield up to isogeny
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over K and a subfield k ⊂ K, A is defined over k up to isogeny if A ∼ A′ ⊗_k K for an abelian variety A′ over k.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II with §3.

items.name: Proposition 3.2 (isogeny classes defined over two subfields)
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k with trdeg(K/k) < ∞, and k₁, k₂ algebraically closed intermediate fields with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k. If A₁/k₁ and A₂/k₂ satisfy A₁ ⊗_{k₁} K ∼ A₂ ⊗_{k₂} K, there is an abelian variety A over k with A₁ ∼ A ⊗_k k₁ and A₂ ∼ A ⊗_k k₂, unique up to isogeny.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. The printed geometric proof assumes independent k₁,k₂ without proving that assumption. Keep the full statement; E18 supplies the defect induction: Reduce by Lemma 3.3 to K=acl(k₁k₂); write k₁=acl(k(c)), k₂=acl(k(b)) for finite tuples and δ=trdeg(k₁/k)+trdeg(k₂/k)−trdeg(k₁k₂/k). For δ=0 use the printed independent-fields proof. For δ>0 choose a k₁-copy τK independent of K over k₁ in an algebraically closed Ω; then K∩τK=k₁ and k₂∩τk₂=k. Transport the isogeny fixing A₁ to obtain A₂∼τA₂ over Ω. Put d₁=trdeg(k₁/k), d₂=trdeg(k₂/k), e=trdeg(k₁k₂/k), a=trdeg(c/k(b,τb)). Independence gives trdeg(k(b,τb,c)/k)=2e−d₁, hence the new defect δ′=2δ−d₁+a, with a≤d₁−δ. Equality would make the loci of c over k₂ and τk₂ equal after extension to acl(k₂τk₂), since both contain the locus over that field with the same dimension. Lemma 3.4 then descends this locus to k, contradicting dim locus=d₁−δ<d₁. Thus 0≤δ′<δ. Induction descends A₂ up to isogeny to k, and Lemma 3.3 over k₁ descends A₁. This uses algebraically closed fields and finite transcendence degrees throughout, but no characteristic-zero hypothesis.

items.name: Lemma 3.3 (isogeny descends to an algebraically closed base)
items.statement: Let A₁, A₂ be abelian varieties over algebraically closed k and K/k any extension. If A₁ ⊗_k K ∼ A₂ ⊗_k K then A₁ ∼ A₂.
items.note: Spread the isogeny over a k-variety S and specialize at a k-point. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 (fields of definition of subvarieties)
items.statement: Let k₁, k₂ be intermediate fields of K/k with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k, Y a variety over k and X ⊂ Y_K a closed subvariety defined over k₁ and over k₂. Then X is defined over k. Linear-algebra core: a K-subspace of V₀ ⊗_k K that descends to k₁ and to k₂ descends to k.
items.note: Proof by uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form, then a limit over finite-dimensional subspaces. Mathlib has Matrix.IsReducedRowEchelon and Tau Ceti computes one (TauCeti.isReducedRowEchelon_rowReduceMatrix), but uniqueness and the descent statement are absent. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Corollary 3.5(i) (smallest field of definition up to isogeny)
items.statement: Let K/k be an extension of algebraically closed fields and A an abelian variety over K. There is an algebraically closed intermediate field k_A of K/k with trdeg(k_A/k) < ∞ such that, for every algebraically closed intermediate k′, A is defined over k′ up to isogeny if and only if k_A ⊆ k′.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Apply Proposition 3.2 with its E18 dependent-fields repair to k′ and k_A over k′∩k_A. Minimize finite transcendence degree as in the paper. The original proof’s independence shortcut cannot be used here.

items.name: Corollary 3.5(ii) (smallest field of definition of a subvariety)
items.statement: For a variety Y over k and a subvariety X ⊂ Y_K there is an algebraically closed intermediate field k_{X⊆Y_K} of K/k with finite transcendence degree over k such that, for every algebraically closed intermediate k′, X is defined over k′ if and only if k_{X⊆Y_K} ⊆ k′.
items.note: Same proof with Lemma 3.4 for Proposition 3.2. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (the field where X becomes special)
items.statement: Let K/k be a field extension with k algebraically closed in K, I(K/k) the set of intermediate fields algebraically closed in K, A an abelian variety over K and X a subvariety of A_{K̄}. There is k_{A,X} ∈ I(K/k) such that for every k′ ∈ I(K/k), X is special for A/K/k′ if and only if k_{A,X} ⊆ k′.
items.note: The statement is correct, but the case tr(A^{K/k})_K ≠ A of the printed proof is wrong; the repair runs the second case over k_A (sourceIssues E1). Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. The preceding algebraic-closure reduction also fails (E17); replace it by: First construct F=k_{A,X} over K̄/k̄, using E18 for Corollary 3.5(i) and E1 for the first case. Let F″ be the algebraic closure inside K̄ of the compositum of all σ(F), σ∈Aut(K̄/K), and set k_{A,X}=F″∩K. No finiteness of the orbit is assumed. F″ is stable under Aut(K̄/K). For x∈F″ all roots of its minimal polynomial over K lie in F″ (including multiplicities in inseparable characteristic), so its coefficients lie in F″∩K. Thus F″ is algebraic over k_{A,X}, which is algebraically closed in K. For relatively algebraically closed k′⊆K, its algebraic closure k̄′ in K̄ is stable under Aut(K̄/K); consequently X is special over k′ iff F⊆k̄′ iff F″⊆k̄′ iff k_{A,X}⊆k′.

items.name: Lemma 3.7, (1)–(2) (generic hyperplane sections as polarizations over k′)
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated with trdeg(K/k) > 1, and (S, M) a polarization with M very ample. There are infinitely many intermediate fields k′ of K/k, algebraically closed in K with trdeg(k′/k) = 1, each with a geometrically integral codimension-1 subvariety H ⊂ S_{k′} such that (1) H is linearly equivalent to M_{k′} and (2) H → S_{k′} → S induces an isomorphism of generic points; after extending k′ to its algebraic closure k̄′ in K̄ and normalizing ν:H̃→H_{k̄′}, the pair (H̃,ν*(M_{k̄′}|_{H_{k̄′}})) is a polarization of Kk̄′/k̄′ in the sense of §1.1.
items.note: k′ = k(s₁/s₀) from a pencil ⟨s₀, s₁⟩ and H the generic member. The proof builds one such k′; the two distinct ones Proposition 3.1 needs come from varying the pencil (sourceIssues E5). Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. E19: geometric integrality gives regularity of K/k′ and integrality of H_{k̄′}. Normalize this geometric generic member, pull back M, and use finite-pullback-ample. Define the displayed height on H by the same intersection formula even before normalization; field-extension invariance and the projection formula for the strict transform give the equal height on H̃. This introduces no Bertini normality hypothesis.

items.name: Lemma 3.7, height inequality
items.statement: For (k′, H) as in Lemma 3.7, any abelian variety A over K, symmetric ample L and subvariety X of A_{K̄}: ĥ^M_L(X) ≥ ĥ^{M_{k′}|_H}_L(X).
items.note: Reduces to ℒ^{dim X+1} · (π*M)^{dim S−1} · 𝒳 ≥ ℒ_H^{dim X+1} · (π_H*M_H)^{dim S−2} · 𝒳*_H: base change to k′, replace one π*M by π⁻¹(H), and drop the effective cycle (𝒳_{k′})_H − 𝒳*_H. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. E19: geometric integrality gives regularity of K/k′ and integrality of H_{k̄′}. Normalize this geometric generic member, pull back M, and use finite-pullback-ample. Define the displayed height on H by the same intersection formula even before normalization; field-extension invariance and the projection formula for the strict transform give the equal height on H̃. This introduces no Bertini normality hypothesis.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (lowering the transcendence degree)
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated with trdeg(K/k) ≥ 2 and A an abelian variety over K. There are intermediate fields k₁, k₂ of K/k, algebraically closed in K with trdeg(k_i/k) = 1, such that for every closed subvariety X of A_{K̄}, the geometric Bogomolov conjecture holds for (A/K/k, X) if it holds for (A_{K k̄₁}/K k̄₁/k̄₁, X) and (A_{K k̄₂}/K k̄₂/k̄₂, X).
items.note: Take two distinct pencils (E5), normalize their geometric generic members (E19), and use the height inequality plus height-base-change. The algebraically closed Proposition 3.6 uses E1 and E18, and its minimal field lies in F₁∩F₂=k; its general form is repaired by E17. E10 corrects the printed missing negation. For the shorter Proposition 3.1 route, work inside K̄ with F_i=acl(k_i). Distinct relatively algebraically closed transcendence-degree-one k_i have F₁∩F₂=k and the F_i are independent. After quotienting by the connected stabilizer and translating the minimal torsion subvariety, Stab⁰(X)=0 and T_X=A. Specialness over each F_i forces the trace onto A, so A is defined over each F_i up to isogeny. Proposition 3.2 in its independent case descends A up to isogeny to k. The isogeny image of X descends to each F_i, since all torsion points of the constant abelian variety lie over k. Lemma 3.4 descends that image to k, giving specialness. This avoids both the general Galois reduction and the dependent-fields induction for the endpoint proof.

items.name: Multi-sections and torsion multi-sections
items.statement: A multi-section of π : 𝒜 → S is a closed integral subscheme 𝒯 finite and flat over S; it is torsion of order m if its class in 𝒜_𝒯(𝒯) is torsion of order m. A torsion multi-section is the Zariski closure of a torsion point of A(K̄), and one of order m lies in 𝒜[m].
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II with Proposition 4.2.

items.name: Proposition 4.2 (numerical class of a torsion multi-section)
items.statement: Let S be a smooth projective curve over a field k, π : 𝒜 → S an abelian scheme of relative dimension g ≥ 1, ℒ a symmetric rigidified line bundle and 𝒯 a torsion multi-section. Then [ℒ]^g ≡ (deg(ℒ_η)/deg(𝒯/S)) [𝒯] as 1-cycles on 𝒜, where deg(ℒ_η) is the degree of ℒ on the generic fibre.
items.note: Both sides vanish against rigidified ℳ (projection formula for [m] and Lemma 4.1(2)); for ℳ = π*N compare degrees. Grushevsky–Zakharov prove the rational-equivalence version over higher-dimensional bases. The printed proof splits ℒ where it means ℳ (sourceIssues E11). Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Use multiplication-degree (A3), the generic-degree projection formula (SF.5), and the projective total space from abelian-scheme-projectivity (A2). The field degree is already recorded at A6/degree-of-an-endomorphism.

items.name: Zhang's fundamental inequality over function fields
items.statement: For a closed subvariety X of A: sup_{U ⊂ X open} inf_{x ∈ U(K̄)} ĥ_L(x) ≥ ĥ_L(X) (Zhang 1995, Thm. 1.10, over number fields; Gubler 2007, Lemma 4.1, over function fields).
items.note: A cited input. RP.5 plans only the number-field Bogomolov route; routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Lemma 5.2 (dense small points force height zero)
items.statement: Let K/k be finitely generated of transcendence degree 1, A/K an abelian variety, L symmetric ample and X ⊂ A_{K̄} closed. If X contains a dense set of small points of A/K/k, then ĥ_L(X) = 0.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Height zero gives dense small points
items.statement: For a closed subvariety Z of A over a function field, ĥ(Z) = 0 if and only if Z(ε) is Zariski dense for all ε > 0 (Gubler 2007, Cor. 4.4: ĥ_L(X) = 0 iff e₁(X, L) = 0).
items.note: Not stated in the paper, but the induction in §5.3 needs it to apply Theorem 1.1 to a component of canonical height 0 (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Yamaki's reduction theorem
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over K with maximal nowhere degenerate abelian subvariety 𝔪 and t = Im(Tr_A). The geometric Bogomolov conjecture holds for A iff it holds for 𝔪 iff it holds for 𝔪/t (Yamaki, J. reine angew. Math. 2018, Thm. 1.5).
items.note: Checked against arXiv:1405.0896v5, Thm. 1.5. The paper calls 𝔪 the maximal abelian subvariety with everywhere good reduction. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 1.1 to conditions (a)–(d)
items.statement: It suffices to prove Theorem 1.1 when (a) trdeg(K/k) = 1, (b) the model S is a smooth projective curve, (c) A has semistable reduction over S, and (d) A has trivial K/k-trace and good reduction over S; moreover X may be assumed defined over K after a finite extension.
items.note: By Proposition 3.1, the semistable reduction theorem and Yamaki's theorem. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: Iterated sums X_m
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, X_m is the image of the addition morphism f_m : X^m → A, (x₁, …, x_m) ↦ x₁ + ⋯ + x_m, and X₀ = {0}. Then dim X_{m−1} ≤ dim X_m ≤ dim X_{m−1} + dim X.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Lemma 5.3 (the sums become a torsion subvariety)
items.statement: Under (a)–(d), with dim X ≥ 1 and X containing a dense set of small points: there is a unique integer r ≥ 1 with dim X_{r−1} < dim X_r and X_r a torsion subvariety of A. After a torsion translation and a finite extension of K, (e): A′ := X_r is an abelian subvariety of A and dim X_{r−1} < dim X_r.
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed lemma omits dim X ≥ 1 (sourceIssues E4). Proof: X′_m = X_m − m x₀ stabilizes at an abelian subvariety B; small points pass from X^r to X_r; heights on B × C force the image of t in C = A/B to have height 0, hence be torsion by trivial trace. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: Relative dimension of the summation map and its jump locus
items.statement: The summation morphism f : X_{r−1} × X → A′ has relative dimension e = dim X_{r−1} + dim X − dim A′ < dim X, and A′_{e+1} = {y ∈ A′ : dim f⁻¹(y) ≥ e + 1} is closed of codimension ≥ 2.
items.note: Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II.

items.name: Proposition 5.4 (torsion fibres have height zero)
items.statement: Under (a)–(e), for every t ∈ A′(K̄)_tor ∖ A′_{e+1}(K̄) of order prime to char k, every irreducible component of the fibre f⁻¹(t) ⊂ (X_{r−1} × X)_{K̄} has canonical height 0 in (A × A)_{K̄}.
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed proposition allows every torsion t, but the proof treats only torsion multi-sections of order prime to the characteristic (sourceIssues E2). Proof: Proposition 2.1 for h : ℬ → 𝒜′, 𝒴 and V = 𝒯 bounds Σ m_i[𝒵_i] by h*[𝒯] · [𝒴]; Proposition 4.2 replaces [𝒯] by a[ℒ_{𝒜′}]^{dim A′}; Lemma 4.1(4) and ĥ(Y) = 0 (Lemma 5.2) force [𝒵_i] · [ℒ_ℬ]^{e+1} = 0. Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. E16 repairs the model step: Use the Néron model 𝒜′_N of A′ and ℬ_N=𝒜×_S𝒜′_N of B. The generic isomorphism A×A′→B⊆A×A is (x,t)↦(x,t−x), with inverse (x,y)↦(x,x+y). Thus the summation h is the second projection, smooth and flat. The arrow ℬ_N→𝒜×_S𝒜 is an extended homomorphism, not an asserted immersion. Take 𝒴 to be the closure of Y in ℬ_N; its map to 𝒜′_N is surjective by properness and generic dominance. Projectivity and symmetric relatively ample rigidified bundles come from abelian-scheme-projectivity. For prime-to-p torsion, 𝒯 is smooth, so Proposition 2.1 and Proposition 4.2 apply, and Lemma 4.1(4) applies to h*ℒ_{𝒜′_N}. Compute heights on ℬ_N using good-reduction-height; height-properties transports small points and height zero back to the generic inclusion B⊆A×A. Use height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height for the function-field height laws, compatible extensions and normalization; these are RP.0 inputs shared with GH19/5–6 and /72.

items.name: §5.3: Theorem 1.1 under (a)–(d), by induction on dim X
items.statement: Under (a)–(d), a closed subvariety X of A_{K̄} with a dense set of small points is a torsion subvariety. For dim X = 0 by Northcott; for dim X > 0, the components of f⁻¹(t) (t as in Proposition 5.4) have height 0 and dimension e < dim X, hence are torsion by induction. So X_{r−1} × X has dense torsion points, and Manin–Mumford for A × A makes it, and hence X, torsion.
items.note: The induction step needs height 0 ⇒ dense small points (item height-zero-small-points; sourceIssues E3). Routed to the uniform-Bogomolov Part II. Use prime-to-p-torsion-density (A3). In §5.3 it supplies the dense set of admissible base points off A′_{e+1} and, after translation, dense all-torsion points in each torsion fibre component.

items.name: Good reduction passes to abelian subvarieties and quotients
items.statement: For S a smooth projective integral curve over algebraically closed k, K=k(S), and A/K of everywhere good reduction, every abelian subvariety A′⊆A and A/A′ has everywhere good reduction. Their Néron models are abelian schemes, and the inclusion A′→A extends to a homomorphism. In characteristic p the extension need not be a closed immersion and the closure of A′ in the Néron model of A need not be an abelian scheme. If its kernel is étale, the generically trivial kernel is trivial, so the proper monomorphism is closed; this applies in characteristic zero.
items.locator: Xie–Yuan v1, proof of Proposition 5.4, p.25, repaired by E16; BLR §7.4 good-reduction criterion and §7.5; shared GH19/80.
items.note: Missing derived theorem, route 5 at R11.5; reuse PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/80. R11.5 already plans isogeny invariance and the Tate-module criterion; R11.1 supplies models and mapping. One proof uses the prime-to-residue-characteristic Tate module of A′ and A/A′ and Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich. Another uses Poincaré reducibility (A6), isogeny invariance and product factors. The existing A6 packet records an imperfect-field proof gap, relevant to K=k(S) in characteristic p; use the Tate-module proof or close that precise supplier gap, never treat it as discharged. Do not identify these models with embedded closures.

items.name: Functoriality, products and comparison of function-field canonical heights
items.statement: For A/K with K=k(S), S a normal projective integral variety over algebraically closed k, fix an ample polarization M. Point canonical heights are additive in symmetric line bundles, satisfy ĥ_{φ*L}(x)=ĥ_L(φ(x)) for a homomorphism φ, and satisfy ĥ_{p₁*L₁⊗p₂*L₂}(x,y)=ĥ_{L₁}(x)+ĥ_{L₂}(y). For symmetric ample L,L′ there are c,C>0 with cĥ_L≤ĥ_{L′}≤Cĥ_L on A(K̄). Changing the ample base polarization, on a common projective model when necessary, likewise preserves dense small points by two-sided comparison. For cycles, the unnormalized mixed canonical height is multilinear and satisfies H_{φ*L₀,…,φ*L_d}(Z)=H_{L₀,…,L_d}(φ_*Z); if φ|_Z is generically finite onto its d-dimensional image, the degree factor cancels after dividing by (d+1)deg_{φ*L}(Z). In particular an isogeny transports normalized subvariety heights with the pulled-back polarization, and transports dense small points. No multilinearity is claimed for degree-normalized subvariety heights.
items.note: Missing, route 1. Share the curve-height API with PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/5–6. All §5 functorial/product applications are over a curve; retain polarized higher-dimensional bases for the definition of small points and §3. Comparison follows by ample differences and nonnegative canonical heights; for base polarizations use a common model and the projection formula. Homomorphic pullback may be nef rather than ample, so the mixed-height extension is needed. This is an input item, not a claim that the RP.0 blueprint has closed its proof.

items.name: Finite and constant field extensions of geometric heights
items.statement: For K=k(S) with S a smooth projective integral curve over algebraically closed k and finite K′/K, put S′=normalization of S in K′. Under Xie–Yuan’s degree-normalized model convention, recomputing the height using S′ gives ĥ_{S′}(x)=[K′:K]ĥ_S(x), and the same scaling for a geometric subvariety with a pulled-back line bundle; the degree includes inseparable degree. This differs from extending a point inside one fixed normalized M_K-field height, which is independent of its field of definition. Under an algebraically closed extension l/k, intersection numbers of base-changed proper schemes and canonical heights of geometrically integral subvarieties are unchanged. With the compatible base-changed models and polarizations, dense small points and specialness are invariant under finite extension of K and extension of algebraically closed constants. For Lemma 3.7, proper intersection degrees also commute with k′→k̄′ and finite birational normalization of the geometrically integral generic member; this supplies the normalized polarization and height comparison.
items.note: Missing, route 1, shared with PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/5–6 and /72. Distinguish changing the base height from merely enlarging the field of definition. For points the projection formula and [K′(x):K]=[K′(x):K′][K′:K] give the scaling. Constant-field invariance for subvariety heights plus the fundamental inequality and height-zero/small-points equivalence supplies the descent of dense small points; trace and specialness base-change belong to RP.1/the existing Part II. SF.4 supplies finite normalization, SF.0 finite pullback of ample bundles, and SF.5 the projection and field-extension formulas. No new general Bertini-normality theorem is assumed.

items.name: Comparison of model heights with M_K-field Néron–Tate heights
items.statement: For K=k(S), S normal projective over algebraically closed k and M ample, use the valuations ord_D at prime divisors D, weighted by deg_M(D), to obtain the product formula. The model intersection height equals the resulting M_K-field height with model metrics. Tate’s limit identifies the canonical height in (1.2) with the canonical-metric Néron–Tate height H_L(X)/((dim X+1)deg_L(X)). For S a curve, the weights of closed points are 1 and the formula agrees with the function-field point height, including the denominator [K(x):K].
items.note: Missing, route 1; share PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/5–6. Preserve Gubler’s unnormalized mixed height until the last division; Theorem 3.4(e) identifies model and local heights, then Theorem 3.6(d) and the Tate limit identify canonical heights. This interface is required before applying Conrad 9.15, Gubler’s inequalities or Yamaki’s height results to Xie–Yuan’s ĥ.

items.name: Density of prime-to-characteristic torsion
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p≥0, the union of A[n](k) over positive n invertible in k is Zariski dense in A. It remains dense after removing any proper closed subset. In characteristic zero every positive n is allowed. A torsion translate of an abelian subvariety has dense torsion points; the translating torsion point may itself have p-power order.
items.locator: Xie–Yuan v1 §1.1 p.3 and §5.3 p.27; E2 prime-to-p restriction; A3 rank and étaleness theorem.
items.note: Missing derived export of A3, route 3. Direct proof avoiding later quotient inputs: let H be the reduced closed subgroup generated as the closure of the prime-to-p torsion and C=H⁰, an abelian subvariety over perfect k. H has finitely many components, say N. Choose n>1 prime to pN. A[n](k)⊆H(k), and n invertible on the finite component group forces A[n](k)⊆C(k). A3 gives n^(2dim A)=#A[n](k)≤#C[n](k)=n^(2dim C), so C=A. The verifier’s alternative quotient proof uses divisibility of C(k) to lift prime-to-p torsion of A/C and requires quotients or Poincaré reducibility from A6; using it inside A3 would import the downstream A6/RP.5. The direct component-count proof avoids that cycle. Translate the dense prime-to-p subgroup to obtain all-torsion density in each torsion coset, not necessarily prime-to-p density in that coset.

items.name: Seesaw for fibrewise trivial line bundles
items.statement: Let π:X→S be proper, flat and of finite presentation, with geometrically integral fibres, over a reduced locally Noetherian base. If an invertible sheaf ℒ restricts trivially to every geometric fibre, then π_*ℒ is invertible, its formation commutes with base change, and the evaluation map π*π_*ℒ→ℒ is an isomorphism. With a section e, ℒ≅π*e*ℒ; a rigidification along e makes it trivial.
items.locator: Xie–Yuan v1, proof of Lemma 4.1(1), p.20; cohomology and base change input.
items.note: Missing, route 3 A1; use proper-flat cohomology and base change from the JacobianChallenge Layer C / AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension supplier. This is the general relative statement, while upstream ModularCurves Layer 2D supplies only its genus-one Poincaré instance and must be reused there. The relative theorem of the cube, once supplied by A1, also proves Lemma 4.1(1) directly. No fibrewise-equality argument over a nonreduced base is asserted.

items.name: Generic-fibre trivial line bundles come from the base
items.statement: Let S be a smooth projective integral curve over a field, π:𝒜→S an abelian scheme, and η its generic point. An invertible sheaf ℒ on 𝒜 with ℒ|_{𝒜_η} trivial is isomorphic to π*N for a line bundle N on S. With a zero-section rigidification it is trivial.
items.note: Missing, route 2 SF.0, one shared theorem with DGH21/29. Here 𝒜 is regular and each closed fibre is an integral reduced Cartier divisor; a rational trivialization yields a vertical divisor, hence a sum of entire fibres π*(s). This is stronger than applying seesaw without checking the special fibres. SF.0 owns the divisor/line-bundle comparison; use SF.5 only for subsequent intersection calculations.

items.name: Degree and flatness of multiplication on an abelian scheme
items.statement: For an abelian scheme 𝒜→S of constant relative dimension g and integer m≠0, [m] is finite locally free of rank |m|^(2g). It is étale when m is invertible on S. On the integral total space over a smooth integral curve, its generic degree is |m|^(2g), including inseparable degree, as required by the projection formula.

items.name: Projectivity and symmetric rigidified ample bundles over a curve
items.statement: If π:𝒜→S is an abelian scheme over a smooth projective integral curve, then π is projective and 𝒜 admits a symmetric, relatively ample invertible sheaf rigidified along the zero section. Thus 𝒜 is projective over the ground field and is smooth over it when S is smooth. A suitable positive power of a symmetric ample bundle on the generic fibre has such an extension.
items.locator: Xie–Yuan v1 §4.3 pp.21–22, Proposition 5.4 p.26; Raynaud, Faisceaux amples XI 1.13/1.3, shared DGH21/26.

items.name: Making a relatively ample bundle ample by a base twist
items.statement: For a projective morphism π:X→S of Noetherian schemes with S projective over a field, π-ample ℒ and an ample N on S, ℒ⊗π*N^r is ample for all sufficiently large r.
items.locator: Xie–Yuan v1, Lemma 4.1(3), p.20; EGA II 4.6.13.
items.note: Planned as part of R09.1 relative ampleness; Lemma 4.1(3) uses this before pulling back by [m]. This does not require or supply a polarization on a general abelian scheme.

items.name: Finite pullback preserves ampleness
items.statement: For a finite morphism f:X→Y of Noetherian schemes and an ample invertible sheaf L on Y, f*L is ample on X. In particular finite normalization preserves the ample bundle of a polarization, and finite multiplication [m], m≠0, preserves ampleness on the total abelian scheme.
items.locator: Xie–Yuan v1, Lemma 4.1(3), p.20 and the normalized Lemma 3.7 repair E19.

This paper's geometric heights go there as a source: projective models, polarizations and integral models of a finitely generated K/k, the naive and canonical heights of subvarieties (Gubler), the quadratic bound, the good-reduction formula of §4.3, and the Northcott property for trivial trace. PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 routed the curve case of these function-field heights to RP.0 in the same way. The K/k-trace joins GH19's trace and Lang–Néron at RP.1. RP.5 plans translates, stabilizers and Manin–Mumford with explicit characteristic hypotheses; this paper supplies the positive-characteristic trivial-trace case (Hrushovski; Pink–Roessler), quotients by abelian subvarieties and the minimal torsion subvariety. Add the function-field functorial/product/comparison laws, compatible finite and constant extensions, and the model/M_K-field comparison. Coalesce RP.0 with GH19/5–6 and the foundation of /72; the latter’s Part II application imports the foundation. Positive-characteristic Manin–Mumford must use an all-torsion theorem such as Scanlon Theorem 2.2, with its trivial-trace specialization, not a prime-to-p-only theorem.

§2 is intersection theory on smooth projective varieties, consuming the Chow groups and intersection products SF.5 plans: Proposition 2.2 (Bertini-type choice of hypersurfaces through V), Lemma 2.3, the proper part of an intersection with Proposition 2.4 (Fulton-type positivity), Lemma 2.5 and Proposition 2.1, together with nef line bundles and the Bertini integrality theorem of Lemma 3.7. The fibre-dimension loci Y_l and the openness of geometric integrality are morphism-level facts for SF.0. The arbitrary-characteristic Rees-algebra pencil blow-up belongs to SF.4; R09.7a has a characteristic-zero enclosing scope and is not a proved all-characteristic supplier. Reuse one construction after its generality is established, and identify LPV.3’s smooth-axis pencil as its special case. SF.0 also gets finite pullback of ample bundles and generic-fibre triviality of line bundles, the latter shared with DGH21/29. SF.5’s existing planned intersection multiplicity input must include the Tor/product comparison and successive-Cartier associativity; no duplicate theory is requested.

Lemma 4.1 is general theory of line bundles on an abelian scheme over a curve. Parts (1)–(2), [m]*ℒ ≃ m²ℒ and torsion restriction to torsion multi-sections, follow from the theorem of the cube in A1. Parts (3)–(4), nefness of symmetric relatively ample bundles, belong with A2's polarization theory. The vocabulary of symmetric and rigidified bundles goes with them. routes.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: uniform Bogomolov and uniform Mordell–Lang
routes.brief: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-YUAN-26, PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26, PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 and PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 under the same id, and their briefs remain binding. Gao–Habegger contributed the geometric Bogomolov conjecture over function fields of curves in characteristic 0. This paper adds the full conjecture: every characteristic and every finite transcendence degree, by a proof that uses no Betti map. Import from RP.0 the function-field heights, canonical heights of subvarieties, the good-reduction formula h_ℒ = ĥ and the Northcott property for trivial trace. Import from RP.1 the K/k-trace, and from RP.5 torsion subvarieties, stabilizers, quotients and Manin–Mumford for trivial trace in every characteristic (Hrushovski; Pink–Roessler). Import from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 Chow groups, nefness and Xie–Yuan's non-proper intersection inequality (Proposition 2.1), and from SF.4 the pencil blow-up. Import rigidified line bundles and Lemma 4.1 from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1–A2, [m] and torsion from A3, Poincaré reducibility from A6, Néron models from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1 and semistable reduction from R11.3. State and prove the results of the inspected Xie–Yuan arXiv v1, with the recorded repairs (the Inventiones text remains uncollated): small points and special subvarieties; §3.1 fields of definition (Proposition 3.2, Lemmas 3.3–3.4, Corollary 3.5); Proposition 3.6 with the corrected first case (sourceIssues E1); Lemma 3.7 with two distinct pencils (E5); Proposition 3.1. Then Yamaki's reduction theorem (Crelle 2018, Theorem 1.5); multi-sections and Proposition 4.2; Zhang–Gubler's fundamental inequality with Lemma 5.2 and its converse (Gubler 2007, Cor. 4.4); X_m and Lemma 5.3 for dim X ≥ 1 (E4); the jump locus A′_{e+1}; Proposition 5.4 for prime-to-p torsion (E2); the §5.3 induction (E3); and Theorem 1.1. Acceptance: a special subvariety tr(Y ⊗ K̄) + T has dense small points. Proposition 4.2 for an elliptic scheme over a curve: any two torsion sections are numerically equivalent, both ≡ [ℒ]/deg ℒ_η. In characteristic 0 over a curve the result agrees with Gao–Habegger's Theorem 1.1. Apply the additional v1 corrections E16–E19: construct the Néron models 𝒜′_N and ℬ_N=𝒜×_S𝒜′_N in Proposition 5.4, with h the flat second projection and 𝒴 the closure there, never the possibly nonsmooth embedded closures; use R11.5 good-reduction-subquotients (shared GH19/80) after R11.1. For Proposition 3.2 use E18’s induction on the transcendence defect to prove the dependent case; Corollary 3.5(i) and E1 then use its full statement. For Proposition 3.6 replace the false field-intersection bijection by E17’s stable compositum of all Galois conjugates, with the minimal-polynomial proof. Proposition 3.1 can instead use the shorter independent transcendence-degree-one argument recorded in its note. In Lemma 3.7 normalize H_{k̄′} and use E19’s projection/base-change equality before invoking a polarization. Import height-properties, height-base-change and model-mk-height from RP.0, seesaw/projectivity from A1/A2, prime-to-p-torsion-density and multiplication-degree from A3, generic-trivial-line-bundle and finite-pullback-ample from SF.0, relative-to-absolute-ample from R09.1 and the all-characteristic pencil construction from SF.4. The §5.3 base points are prime-to-p torsion; torsion inside the resulting translated components may have p-primary part. Derive Theorem 5.1 from an all-torsion Manin–Mumford theorem, including Scanlon’s Theorem 2.2. Acceptance additionally checks: a finite curve cover of degree d rescales the relative geometric height by d; constant extension preserves it; the normalized pencil gives the same height; the Néron-model projection is flat in characteristic p even when the extended inclusion is not closed. These are source-input specifications; owning blueprint jobs close and test their proofs.

PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 already routes the geometric Bogomolov conjecture (characteristic 0, curves) to this Part II, and the pending design DESIGN-HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII folds all Part IIs of this parent. sourceIssues.reason: The converse fails. Take char k ≠ 2, K an algebraic closure of k(s, t), k′ the algebraic closure of k(s) in K, and A = E ⊗_{k′} K with E : y² = x(x−1)(x−s). A has trivial K/k-trace (j(E) ∉ k), so this is the first case, and k_A = k′. Let P ∈ A(K) have x(P) = t and X = {P}. Then Stab⁰(X) = 0, and T_X = A because P is not torsion (torsion points lie in E(k′)). The printed claim makes X special for A/K/k′, but specialness would give P ∈ E(k′) + A_tor = E(k′), whereas x(P) = t ∉ k′. The proposition itself holds by the corrected argument, and Proposition 3.1 uses only its statement.

review.reason: Confirmed on the page image of p. 16. The printed claim 'X is special for A/K/k′ iff k_{A,X} ⊆ k′' with k_{A,X} = k_A fails in the 'if' direction. Example: take k′ ⊇ k_A, so that A ∼ A₀ ⊗_{k′} K; let C ⊂ A₀ be a curve over k′ with trivial stabilizer that generates A₀, and X = C_K + P with P ∈ A₀(K) ∖ A₀(k′). Then Stab⁰(X) = 0 and T_X = A. sourceIssues.correction: First construct F=k_{A,X} over K̄/k̄, using E18 for Corollary 3.5(i) and E1 for the first case. Let F″ be the algebraic closure inside K̄ of the compositum of all σ(F), σ∈Aut(K̄/K), and set k_{A,X}=F″∩K. No finiteness of the orbit is assumed. F″ is stable under Aut(K̄/K). For x∈F″ all roots of its minimal polynomial over K lie in F″ (including multiplicities in inseparable characteristic), so its coefficients lie in F″∩K. Thus F″ is algebraic over k_{A,X}, which is algebraically closed in K. For relatively algebraically closed k′⊆K, its algebraic closure k̄′ in K̄ is stable under Aut(K̄/K); consequently X is special over k′ iff F⊆k̄′ iff F″⊆k̄′ iff k_{A,X}⊆k′.
